transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Horizon - Head of InfoSec), Marcus Reed (Horizon - Cloud Architect), Daniel Park (Procurement), Lina Gomez (Legal)

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jamie collins from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. priya from our solutions engineering team is with me, she'll handle the technical bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: good thanks, a bit pressed but ready. main goal today is to get through the SIG questionnaire and understand what evidence you'll be able to provide.
[00:14] Jamie: perfect. quick agenda - we'll walk the SIG/CAIQ items you flagged, highlight where we have attestation docs (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001), cover SSO and RBAC, audit logs, encryption and key management and data residency/VPC options. then capture action items. sound good?
[00:27] Marcus: yep, and procurement and legal might ask a couple of questions too.
[00:31] Daniel: quick ask - can you point to where we get the SOC report and any pen test summaries?
[00:36] Jamie: sure, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO attestation. pen test summary is okay - we have a redacted exec summary, i'll put that in the folder. i'll upload links after the call.
[00:44] Priya: starting with the SIG matrix - i'll go section by section. feel free to interrupt. first, identity and access management, questions around SSO, SCIM, roles, least privilege. we support SAML 2.0 for SSO, OIDC for new integrations, and SCIM for user provisioning. our RBAC model has org / project / role scopes.
[01:02] Aisha: can you show the RBAC screen or an example role mapping?
[01:06] Priya: yes, i can prepare screenshots. right now i don't have the console up in this meeting share, but i'll include a few screenshots in the evidence pack. note - sometimes the transcript tool spells scim as "skim" so just flag, ha.
[01:17] Marcus: for our audit requirements we need proof of role change approvals and a history of permission escalation events. how long are logs retained?
[01:24] Priya: default audit logs are retained 90 days in the hosted plan, with extended retention available as an add-on (we can retain up to 7 years on dedicated/private). audit logs include API calls, auth events, role changes, and admin actions. we can export to your SIEM via secure streaming.
[01:40] Lina: what format are logs in and can we get them in our S3 bucket?
[01:44] Priya: yes, logs are JSON lines, and we support pushing to an s3 bucket or to syslog/elk. we'll include schema docs.
[01:50] Jamie: quick note on evidence - we'll put a sample log extract (redacted) and a log schema in the shared folder.
[01:58] Aisha: encryption and KMS - do you manage keys or can we bring our own? any HSM support?
[02:03] Priya: both. by default we manage keys, encrypted at rest and in transit. we integrate with customer-managed KMS for the private/dedicated offering; you can bring keys from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. HSM-backed keys (via KMS) are supported for private deployments. i'll add the KMS integration doc and screenshots of the key rotation settings.
[02:21] Daniel: rotation policy - what's the default rotation cadence?
[02:24] Priya: rotation is 90 days by default for service keys; customer-managed keys follow your KMS policy. we rotate ephemeral keys for sessions more frequently. i'll share a policy excerpt.
[02:33] Marcus: about data residency - we need EU-only data handling for EU customers. can you guarantee regionally isolated deployments?
[02:40] Jamie: yes - hosted regions can be pinned, and for stricter requirements we offer dedicated capacity in-region or our private deployment. data residency controls, VPC peering, and ingress/egress whitelisting are available. we'll document options and lead times.
[02:55] Aisha: do you offer an on-prem air-gapped option?
[02:58] Jamie: yes, private on-prem package exists; that's more of a licensing + deployment project with our infra team. we'll include a short note and a contact if you want to explore.
[03:06] Priya: moving on to secure development / vulnerabilities - SOC 2 covers change management and vulnerability management. we have an annual third-party pentest and weekly SAST scans. the SIG question about patch windows - we patch criticals within 48 hours for managed infra. non-managed customers have policies we can share.
[03:24] Lina: legal will want the SLA and incident response playbook. is incident notification automated?
[03:28] Jamie: yes, we have incident response runbooks; customers get notifications via email and optional webhooks. severity-based SLAs are in the contract. we'll attach the IR summary and the SLA page.
[03:37] Aisha: on the SIG question about breach notification timelines - what's your commitment?
[03:41] Jamie: we notify customers within 24 hours of confirmed incidents affecting customer data, with follow-ups. we'll include our policy excerpt.
[03:49] Marcus: can you share an example of audit logs showing an admin role elevation followed by a rollback? we need to show traces in a compliance audit.
[03:56] Priya: yes - i'll pull a redacted example showing timestamped events, actor IDs, and IPs. note that some fields are hashed for PII reasons; we'll show the mapping.
[04:07] Daniel: procurement asks about subcontractors and data flow - where's data stored, who has access?
[04:13] Jamie: in hosted mode data is stored in the selected cloud region; our sub-processors list will be provided. access to customer data is on a need-to-know basis with role approvals and audit trails. dedicated/private customers get stricter controls.
[04:26] Aisha: about the SIG controls for encryption-in-transit - what ciphers and TLS versions do you support?
[04:31] Priya: we enforce TLS 1.2 and 1.3, strong ciphers only. mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints. i'll include the TLS and cipher list in the evidence set.
[04:41] Jamie: question from procurement - any vendor risk questionnaires you've seen commonly fail us on?
[04:46] Priya: sometimes questions around multi-tenancy isolation and encryption key ownership; we usually address that with docs and architecture diagrams. also data residency and long-term retention need explicit confirmation.
[04:56] Lina: legal wants indemnity language and data processing addendum - do you have a standard DPA?
[04:59] Jamie: yes, we have a standard DPA and can negotiate enterprise clauses. i'll send the DPA and the redwood privacy notice link.
[05:08] Aisha: SIG v4 specifically asks about RBAC separation of duties - can you show how to enforce separation?
[05:14] Priya: yes, our RBAC supports least privilege, configurable approval workflows, and we can enforce separation across roles. we'll include sample role templates and a mapping doc.
[05:25] Marcus: integration to our IdP - SAML and SCIM are great, but do you support Just-In-Time provisioning?
[05:30] Priya: we support SCIM provisioning and JIT for OIDC flows. SCIM sync delta is available; i'll include SCIM schema and example mapping.
[05:38] Jamie: tiny note - sometimes the auto-transcript mangles scim as "skim" or "scum"; apologies if you see that in the export.
[05:45] Daniel: back to audit - are logs tamper-evident?
[05:48] Priya: logs are write-once in the managed service with immutability markers; for dedicated/private we can enable append-only systems and S3 object lock on exports. we'll provide a description and sample config.
[05:59] Aisha: evidence for ISO 27001 - do you have the certificate and scope?
[06:03] Jamie: yes, we will provide the ISO certificate PDF and the scope page.
[06:08] Lina: any SOC comments about encryption at rest?
[06:11] Priya: we encrypt at rest using AES-256. keys are rotated and can be customer-managed. details will be in the KMS doc.
[06:18] Marcus: technical deep dive question - how do you handle prefix caching and KV cache in the runtime? any implications on data leakage between customers?
[06:26] Priya: good question - we shard caches per tenant and enforce strict namespace isolation. the runtime uses per-tenant keying and boundary checks to prevent cross-tenant leakage. sometimes the transcript spells KV as "K-V" or "kay-vee" in the export. we'll include an architecture diagram.
[06:43] Aisha: are there third-party audit logs for access to key material?
[06:47] Priya: yes - access to KMS keys is logged by the KMS provider, and we surface those events in our audit logs; additionally, we can provide proof of role approvals for key access.
[06:56] Jamie: let's talk timeline: looks like horizon is aiming for vendor approval by end of month. what do you need from us to get through the procurement checklist?
[07:04] Daniel: SOC report, DPA, SLA, pen test summary, evidence screenshots for RBAC and KMS, and data residency confirmation.
[07:11] Jamie: we'll deliver those items into a shared folder. i'll create a folder in our secure drive and post links in the follow-up email.
[07:18] Priya: last part - on the SIG matrix there are several 'partial' answers where we depend on customer config (e.g., encryption key ownership). we will flag those as "customer-configurable" and add guidance text.
[07:30] Aisha: for the CAIQ items that ask for automation of evidence, do you have an API to pull logs/evidence?
[07:36] Priya: yes, we have an export API that can pull logs, role history, and config snapshots; we'll include API docs and an example curl.
[07:44] Lina: any legal gotchas we should know about?
[07:47] Jamie: the main ones are standard - subprocessor lists, data transfer mechanisms, and limitation of liability. we can escalate specific contract asks to our legal team.
[07:56] Marcus: would like an explicit note in the SIG where you state that dedicated/private deployments are isolated and keys remain customer-owned.
[08:02] Priya: we'll mark those responses as "Dedicated/Private: customer-key ownership" and include the technical config steps.
[08:10] Jamie: recap of next steps: i'll upload SOC 2 and ISO docs, pen test summary, and DPA; priya will assemble the technical evidence (RBAC screenshots, KMS rotation, audit log sample, SCIM schema); we'll propose a follow-up on May 22 to walk through the evidence.
[08:24] Aisha: that works.
[08:26] Daniel: also need procurement to get a copy of pricing and an outline of dedicated vs hosted costs if we decide to pin region.
[08:32] Jamie: i'll include a high-level cost sheet and note that dedicated capacity pricing is a separate line item - sales will follow up if you want a detailed quote.
[08:39] Lina: can you also provide contact for privacy officer?
[08:42] Jamie: yes, i'll include an email for our privacy officer.
[08:45] Priya: action items reiterated: i'll deliver screenshots and the KMS docs; jamie will deliver attestations and legal docs; we'll send a calendar invite for the evidence walk-through.
[08:56] Aisha: thanks, appreciate the clarity - we'll review the materials and send any follow-up questions.
[09:00] Jamie: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Links / references to be included in follow-up:
- SOC 2 Type II (redwood-s3-link)
- ISO 27001 certificate (redwood-s3-link)
- Pen test executive summary (redwood-s3-link)
- Shared evidence folder: https://redwood-secure-sso.example.com/horizon-evidence
- SIG/CAIQ completed draft (attached PDF)
- SCIM schema and sample provisioning mapping (attached)
- KMS integration doc and rotation policy excerpt (attached)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (SCIM -> skim), some proper nouns garbled.
